route_title: Optimization of SiO2/TiO2 Bilayer Order and Thickness for Broadband AR

route_snapshot.title: Optimization of SiO2/TiO2 Bilayer Order and Thickness for Broadband AR
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system with indices n_air < n_SiO2 < n_TiO2 > n_glass, the stack ordering Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass yields a lower global minimum mean reflectance than Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass because the intermediate SiO2 layer reduces the initial impedance mismatch at the air interface more effectively than starting with the high-index TiO2.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Impedance matching in multilayer optics suggests that arranging layers in ascending order of refractive index (or close to it) minimizes Fresnel reflections at each interface. Placing the lower index SiO2 (n=1.46) adjacent to air (n=1.0) creates a smaller step change than placing TiO2 (n=2.40) adjacent to air, potentially broadening the low-reflectance bandwidth despite the non-ideal final step from TiO2 to Glass (n=1.52).
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thicknesses must remain within 40 nm to 160 nm bounds
exactly one layer of each material permitted
theory_basis: Fresnel equations for normal incidence reflection at dielectric interfaces
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for calculating coherent superposition of fields in stratified media
Quarter-wave transformer theory generalized for broadband minimization via numerical optimization
expected_advantages: Directly tests the theoretically preferred material ordering for impedance grading
Concentrates the limited 64-evaluation budget on refining thicknesses for the most promising topology rather than splitting resources between two topologies
Provides a clear baseline; if this optimal ordering fails to meet the target, the reverse ordering is unlikely to succeed given the larger initial index mismatch
known_risks: The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) might unexpectedly perform better due to specific phase cancellation effects at the substrate interface not captured by simple impedance arguments
The thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent the formation of ideal quarter-wave or half-wave conditions for the entire 450-700 nm band
Constant index assumption may introduce errors if actual material dispersion is significant, though the problem statement mandates constant indices
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar four-medium stack: Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2 (Gao), n=1.46), Layer 2 (TiO2 (Siefke), n=2.40), Substrate (Glass, n=1.52). The optimization must vary the thickness of the SiO2 (Gao) layer and the TiO2 (Siefke) layer independently, subject to hard bounds of 40 nm to 160 nm for each. The objective function is the arithmetic mean of the power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), calculated at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm inclusive. Use a deterministic optimizer with seed 17, allowing a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Report the best candidate's thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.

compilation_rationale: User requests constant-index layers and s-polarization at normal incidence. Fixed order SiO2/TiO2 declared for Experiment 1. Thickness bounds 40-160 nm applied. Mean reflectance minimization mapped to objective. Seed 17 and eval limit noted in rationale as execution constraints, not task parameters.

route_title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2 Bilayer with Analytical Quarter-Wave Initialization

route_snapshot.title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2 Bilayer with Analytical Quarter-Wave Initialization
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: Swapping the layer order to TiO2 (high index) adjacent to air and SiO2 (low index) adjacent to glass, combined with an initialization based on the analytical quarter-wave condition at the spectral center (575 nm), will allow the gradient optimizer to converge to a distinct local minimum with a lower broadband mean reflectance than the SiO2-first configuration found in Round 1.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Impedance matching via a high-to-low index transition (Air->TiO2->SiO2->Glass) often provides a smoother effective index gradient than low-to-high for this specific substrate/incident pair. Initializing near the theoretical single-wavelength optimum ($d = \λ_c / 4n$) reduces the risk of the optimizer settling in a shallow local minimum far from the physical resonance condition.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of TiO2 and one layer of SiO2
theory_basis: Quarter-wave antireflection condition: $n_1 d_1 = n_2 d_2 = \λ_c/4$ for zero reflectance at a single wavelength.
Effective medium theory suggesting high-index-first ordering may better match the large Air-Glass index jump.
expected_advantages: Potential to escape the local minimum found in the SiO2-first topology.
Analytical initialization provides a physically grounded starting point closer to the global optimum.
known_risks: The TiO2-first order might yield a higher minimum reflectance due to stronger Fresnel reflections at the first interface if not perfectly tuned.
The quarter-wave thicknesses for 575 nm might fall outside the 40-160 nm bounds or require scaling that distorts the broadband response.
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar stack: Incident Medium (Air, n=1.0) | Layer 1 (TiO2, n=2.40, lossless) | Layer 2 (SiO2, n=1.46, lossless) | Substrate (Glass, n=1.52, lossless). Constraints: Both layer thicknesses must be between 40 nm and 160 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (5 nm steps). Optimization Settings: Use seed 17, maximum 64 solver evaluations. Initialize the optimizer with the analytical quarter-wave thicknesses for the center wavelength 575 nm: initial_thickness_TiO2 = 575/(4*2.40) nm, initial_thickness_SiO2 = 575/(4*1.46) nm. If these initial values fall outside the [40, 160] nm bounds, clamp them to the nearest bound before starting the optimization run. Report the final optimized thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
route_snapshot.revision_reason: Feedback directive requested swapping the layer order (TiO2 first) and using an analytical quarter-wave initialization at 575 nm to explore a different region of the design space compared to Round 1's SiO2-first random/gradient start.

compilation_rationale: The request specifies constant indices, overriding registry dispersion. Two layer orders are permitted; Experiment 1 fixes the order TiO2/SiO2 as requested in the primary instruction. Bounds [40, 160] nm are applied. The optimization targets mean reflectance minimization with a soft preference for <0.03. Seed and evaluation limits are mapped to optimizer settings.
